rows.text: September 7, 2007
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
The domestic economy seems likely to maintain its upward trend.
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
While exports continue to post robust growth, domestic demand is showing a steady increase, led by consumption.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
Consumer price inflation remains stable despite the rise in international oil prices.
The upward trend of real estate prices has been blunted.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
In the financial markets, there is ample liquidity and financial institutions' lending continues to show a steady increase.
Meanwhile, financial market price variables have shown increased volatility, affected by the recent international financial market unrest.
The domestic economy seems likely to maintain its upward trend.
While exports continue to post robust growth, domestic demand is showing a steady increase, led by consumption.
The future level of the policy rate will continue to be decided after overall consideration of the movements of prices, economic activity and the financial markets, as shown by the latest indicators.
Consumer price inflation remains stable despite the rise in international oil prices.
The upward trend of real estate prices has been blunted.
In the financial markets, there is ample liquidity and financial institutions' lending continues to show a steady increase.
Meanwhile, financial market price variables have shown increased volatility, affected by the recent international financial market unrest.
The future level of the policy rate will continue to be decided after overall consideration of the movements of prices, economic activity and the financial markets, as shown by the latest indicators.
